lawyer:
AKM Badrudduza, Advocate—For Petitioners. 
Jashimuddin Ahmed, Advocate—For the Respondents.
parties:
Amina Alam and others ------ petitioners
vs
Shotodol Property Development Ltd and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: There is nothing on record to convince this Court that the respondent Nos. 3, 4 and 5 in entering into contractual relationships with other parties by exploiting the Company's goodwill and securing the incorporation of another entity, a rival both in name and business to the Company, actually acted in good faith and in furtherance of the interests of the Company and the shareholders. Relying on the ratio of the judgment in Syed Al-Nesar A/Ivied vs Nafisa Chowdhury reported in 53 DLR (AD). 83, the learned Advocate for the petitioners Mr AKM Badrudduza has established that certain fundamental breaches of the rules have exposed the aggrandizing and appropriating devices of the respondent Nos. 3, 4 and 5 in denial of the Company's entitlements as justify the filing of this Application. He submits satisfactorily that the terms of the agreement dated 7-3-2007 substantiates the petitioners' fears that acts as this were undertaken by the respondent Nos. 3, 4 and 5 solely for unlawful gain to the detriment of the Company. It is in that light that Mr Badrudduza has drawn this Court's attention to Article 39 of the Articles and the interpretation given it by the BoD in its resolution dated 10-4-2008. That resolution has, however, appeared before this Court in an interpolated form, such interpolation being explained on behalf of the petitioners as the handiwork, of the respondent No. 2, then incumbent Chairman. Upon the signing the adopted resolution, the respondent No. 2 is said to have proceeded behind the back of the BoD to 'modify' the same. Such 'modification' was clearly undertaken in a blatant disregard of the Articles and rules of management and the respondent No. 2 eventually resigned as Chairman. Of concern to this Court is the resolution's adoption on 10-4-2008 for operating bank accounts in a manner discordant with Article 39 in that it excludes the Chairman's rule at the invocation of the discretion granted to the BoD under Article 39 to change the account operation signatory. Notwithstanding, that this resolution has never been confirmed by the BoD, a precedent was set of arbitrary exercise of discretion under Article 39 in a manner clearly oppressive of other shareholders. The petitioners apprehend that the present for-1n-illation of Article 39 allowing the BoD discretion to change the signatory of bank operation as deemed fit unduly exposes the Company to whimsical, capricious and arbitrary decisions of a browbeaten BoD at the behest of the respondent Nos. 3, 4 and 5 exerting their superior voting authority. The prayer, therefore, is to cancel that provision in Article 39 as presently enables the BoD at its discretion to change the signatory for bank account operation.
